lead.hed: USNI: Abraham Lincoln operates with Australian frigates in the South China Sea
lead.insight: USNI News, Tuesday: USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) recently operated with Royal Australian Navy frigates HMAS Perth and HMAS Stuart in the South China Sea, Australia’s Department of Defence announced. The frigates supported the Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group during its transit. Partner transit, not a combat action.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Daniel Kimmelman · DVIDS 9477203 · Public domain · An MH-60R Sea Hawk from HSM-71 prepares to land on USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72) in the South China Sea, Jan. 8, 2026.

political.hed: Defense News: Italian NATO jet shoots down a drone over Lithuania
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday from Siauliai: Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto said an Italian NATO fighter shot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace that most probably came from Russia. Lithuania said the aircraft entered from Belarus after midnight and was downed near Pratkunai. Origin still under debris exam; Russia had not commented.

political.hed: Defense News: Ukraine says it opened a Donetsk offensive north of the fortress belt
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: Brig. Gen. Andrii Biletskyi said Ukraine’s 3rd Army Corps launched operation Vivaldi north of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, clearing 75 square kilometers of Russian infiltration groups and recapturing 10 more, with Serednie fully under Ukrainian control. Commander claim; Reuters could not independently verify the lines.

political.hed: Defense News: Chinese captains call Marine Stand-In Forces a near-seas threat
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: a U.S. Naval War College translation of a 2023 Military Art article by PLA Navy captains Yue Zhiqiang, Wang Li, and Li Jinqiao argues Marine Stand-In Forces would erode China’s land-enabled sea-denial and complicate island-chain breakout. Journal analysis from 2023, published in English this summer — not a new PLA order.

tech.hed: Defense News: Space Force aims to add 10,000 guardians in five years
tech.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: STARCOM commander Maj. Gen. James E. Smith said the service’s target is 10,000 more guardians over five years, with a large first-year jump, and more than 200 instructor billets to absorb the surge. STARCOM’s own release matches the training-pipeline numbers. Personnel target, not a funded end-strength law.

tech.hed: Defense News: Air Force panel says counter-drone AI is a trust problem
tech.insight: Defense News, Monday from the Air, Space & Cyber Conference: Epirus CTO Michael Hiatt told a counter-UAS panel that the ground problem is magazine doubt, not cost asymmetry, and that trust in directed-energy systems has to be built before operators will fire. Panel argument, not a new Air Force acquisition decision.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Recovering the official reading of the Fourteenth Amendment
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Tuesday: James Patterson talks with David Upham about Taking American Citizenship Seriously, arguing that many legal theories about the Fourteenth Amendment are not rooted enough in the amendment’s history and text. Podcast, not a Supreme Court ruling.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Why politicians stay indebted
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Tuesday: Theodore Dalrymple argues public debt keeps a political class indispensable, because present benefits buy votes more easily than paying the bill. Essay, not a Treasury print.
